brief.text: A machine shop that makes 60 machined aluminium bike-light housings an hour, laid out as in the attached sketch on a 45 by 30 metre floor. Aluminium bar stock arrives at the west dock, is checked in at a receiving desk and stored on pallet racks, cut to length on a metal-cutting bandsaw, turned on CNC lathes (about 4 minutes a part), milled on CNC milling machines (about 9 minutes a part), tumbled in vibratory deburring machines, cleaned in a parts washer, measured on coordinate measuring machines, serial-numbered on a fibre laser marking machine, then packed and palletised for shipping at the east dock. Parts move between steps on conveyors.

requirements.name: Bike-light housing machine shop
requirements.summary: A 45 by 30 m machine shop producing 60 machined aluminium bike-light housings per hour from bar stock via sawing, CNC turning, CNC milling, deburring, washing, CMM inspection, laser marking, and packing.
assumptions: Station footprints, power draws, and cycle times for receiving, storage, sawing, deburring, washing, CMM inspection, laser marking, packing, and shipping are taken from the research notes where not stated in the brief.
One operator is assigned per station type by default.
Only the aqueous conveyor parts washer requires a direct mains water connection.
Power and water utility entries are on the north wall and receiving/shipping docks on the west/east walls as shown in the sketch.

research.summary:
WORKING NOTES: BIKE-LIGHT HOUSING MACHINE SHOP (45m x 30m)

1. MATERIAL FLOW & DEPARTMENTS
Material flows West to East through: Receiving & Storage -> Sawing -> Turning -> Milling -> Deburring -> Washing -> Inspection -> Laser Marking -> Packing & Shipping.

2. DEPARTMENT DETAILS (Process | Equipment | Cycle Time/Unit | Footprint | Power)

- Receiving & Storage: Unload aluminium bar stock, check in, store on racks. | West dock, receiving desk, pallet racks, forklift (estimate). | ~60 s/part equivalent (estimate). | ~3.0 x 2.5 m per station (estimate). | ~0 kW (electric/fuel forklift, estimate).
- Sawing: Cut bar stock to billet length. | Automatic horizontal metal-cutting bandsaw. | ~30 s (estimate). | ~1.9 x 1.2 m. | 1.5–2.2 kW.
- Turning: Turn housing profiles (5 stations). | CNC lathes (e.g., Haas ST-10). | 240 s (4 min). | ~3.2 x 1.8 m. | 11.2 kW (15 hp spindle).
- Milling: Mill fins, slots, and mounts (11 stations). | CNC vertical mills (e.g., Haas VF-2). | 540 s (9 min). | ~2.5 x 2.0 m. | 22.4 kW (30 hp spindle).
- Deburring: Tumble parts with media to remove burrs (2 stations). | Vibratory bowl deburring machines (250–350 L). | ~60 s/part equivalent in batch (estimate). | ~1.3 x 1.3 m. | 3.7–5.5 kW.
- Washing: Aqueous spray wash, rinse, and air blow-off. | Conveyor pass-through parts washer. | ~45 s (estimate). | ~3.0 x 1.5 m (estimate). | ~12 kW (pumps and heaters, estimate).
- Inspection: Probe 3D tolerances against CAD (2 stations). | Bridge Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMMs). | ~90 s (estimate). | ~1.5 x 1.5 m (estimate). | 0.7 kW max.
- Laser Marking: Engrave serial numbers on bare aluminium. | 50 W fibre laser marking machine. | ~15 s (estimate). | ~1.0 x 1.0 m (estimate). | ~0.8 kW (wall-plug, estimate).
- Packing & Shipping: Pack housings, palletise, load at East dock. | Packing station, palletiser, East dock. | ~30 s (estimate). | ~3.0 x 2.0 m (estimate). | ~0.5 kW (estimate).

3. INTER-STEP MATERIAL MOVEMENT
Parts move between sawing, machining, deburring, washing, inspection, marking, and packing on powered belt or roller conveyors. Bar stock moves from the West dock to racks and the bandsaw via forklift (estimate).

4. PLANT BENCHMARKS
- Typical Output: 60 housings/hour (1 part/minute, balanced by 5 lathes at 4 min/part and 11 mills at 9 min/part).
- Typical Floor Area: 1,350 sq m (45 m x 30 m), standard for a 16-CNC-machine production cell with conveyors, aisles, and dock staging (estimate).
